reevaluation: Stands unchanged, and I re-confirmed the review's most consequential claim about PR #26990 against the PR's current diff (it was pushed again on 2026-08-18, after the review). The PR does refactor the per-field builder into a new helper buildScalarFieldFilter, and that helper still contains the faulty line verbatim: 'const valueSchema = attributeTypeToFilterValue(attr)' followed by 'Object.fromEntries(FILTER_OPERATORS.map((op) => [op, valueSchema.optional()]))'. So merging #26990 would carry $null/$notNull forward broken, exactly as the review said, and would also extend the same bug to nested component fields. Nothing new was filed. The one genuinely new neighbour is issue #27395 (2026-08-17, open, severity: high, status: confirmed), a different MCP tool-schema defect; it is not a duplicate but it establishes that this class of report is accepted and triaged quickly.
policyBasis: CONTRIBUTING.md: "Strapi is using GitHub issues to manage bugs. We keep a close eye on them. Before filing a new issue, try to ensure your problem does not already exist." .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml sets blank_issues_enabled: false, so the report must go through BUG_REPORT.yml, whose required fields are Node version, package manager + version, exact Strapi version ("Latest" is not a valid response), OS, database, JS/TS, Bug Description, Steps to Reproduce, Expected Behavior, and both confirmation checkboxes.
notes: Worth a short comment on PR #26990 as well as the issue, since that PR relocates the exact faulty line into buildScalarFieldFilter and its author can fix it in place. Scope for the report: broken on every scalar attribute type except boolean, not just on string fields (integer/decimal fields get number | number[] and reject true the same way); accepted only where valueSchema is z.boolean(). Two claims in the review are code-path readings with no evidence file behind them, so mark them as such or drop them: that {"$null": "true"} works via parseType's TRUTHY_INPUTS, and that {"$null": null} force-casts to false and silently runs whereNotNull (the inverse of the request). The second is the more damaging of the pair and is worth reproducing before it goes in a bug report.
